summary: What worked: shortening the sliding-window attention span on the 'S' layers from seq/2 to seq/4 is a one-constant change worth -0.0032 on the width-640 base (0.984898 -> 0.981666) and it stacks cleanly with width, giving the cell best 0.979960 at dim 768 / depth 8 / MLP 4x / batch 2**18. Long-range capacity is not the binding constraint at this scale: the two full-context 'L' layers suffice, and the freed FLOPs buy ~9% more tokens in the fixed 300s. What did not work: my fixed-FLOPs depth-for-MLP-width trade. It looked good at dim 512 (depth 8->10 with MLP 4x->3x, -0.0011 at batch 2**19 and -0.0013 at 2**18) but it was really just compensating for a capacity-starved narrow model - at dim 640 the same reshape was a net loss (0.986335 vs 0.984898), and pushing it further to depth 12 / MLP 2x at exactly equal params and FLOPs was clearly worse (0.988923). MLP hidden must stay at >=3x d_model, and depth is not the axis to spend on. What I would try next: the window lever is not exhausted - test SHORT_WINDOW_DIV 8 and a window pattern with only one 'L' layer, at dim 768; then re-spend the savings on width (896 needs a memory-lean loss head, which crashed for a peer at 1475c37). Also worth a run: shortening windows should shift the batch-size optimum, so re-check 2**19 at dim 768 with seq/8 windows.
